title: Protocol for Relative Hydrodynamic Assessment of Tri-leaflet Polymer Valves
protocol: Design an assembly to accommodate a tri-leaflet valve geometry.
Fabricate a valve holder to suture in the valve leaflets.
Create a tube to house the valve holder and secure it onto the pulse duplicator system.
Cleanse the entire loop system using soap solution and water, including replacing any degraded tubes.
Calibrate instruments connected to the loop with 1% saline solution.
Repeat calibration prior to using blood-analog glycerin solution.
Obtain 4 fresh pig hearts with intact aortas.
Rinse the heart with deionized water.
Place the heart in a receptacle filled with 1% antimycotic/antibiotic and sterile PBS solution.
Transport the heart on ice to the hydrodynamic testing laboratory.
Place the heart in a dissecting pan.
Remove the pericardium carefully.
Position the heart with the ventral side facing you.
Visually inspect and identify the four chambers of the heart.
Locate the aortic arch on the intact aorta.
Cut across horizontally at approximately 0.75 inches below the annulus to separate the heart into two halves.
Isolate the intact aorta still attached to the left ventricular tissue segment carefully.
Examine the aortic valve located in the aortic root for damage or calcification.
Split the aorta at approximately 1 inch above the annulus.
Separate the left ventricular tissue segment below the annulus to isolate the aortic valve.
Place the heart valve inside the valve holder such that the base of each valve aligns with the base of the post holder.
Secure the valve temporarily at each post with a paper clip without damaging the commissures or cusps.
Insert the suture into the needle.
Begin suturing at the bottom of the valve holder by passing the needle through the first hole from outside to inside.
Continue suturing in a looping fashion vertically up the posts of the valve holder.
Suture along the circumference of the holder and secure with additional suture around the tips of the holder posts.
Remove paper clips when the valve is completely secured using sutures to the 3 posts and at the circumference of the valve holder.
Set heart rate of pulse duplicator system to 70 beats per minute.
Select a flow waveform to drive the pump, such as the S35 waveform for all hydrodynamic tests.
Turn on amplifier and piston pump.
Warm up the system for 15 minutes.
Place bi-leaflet valve in the aortic position.
Smear vacuum grease on all junctions where leaks could occur.
Pour glycerin/saline liquid into the atrial compartment.
Prepare saline solution using common salt dissolved in deionized water at a concentration of 9 mg/ml (weight/volume).
Turn on the flow transducer placed in the aortic position.
Calibrate the pump according to instructions from ViVitro Labs Inc. software.
Proceed with calibration of each flow and pressure under the calibrate tab in the ViVitest software.
Start the pump at low rpm until fluid fills the aortic compartment.
Check for leaks and use additional vacuum grease if necessary.
Turn two stop-cocks (aortic and ventricular transducers) to open position.
Increase the pump's rpm until stroke volume reaches 80 ml/beat.
Allow the system to run for 10 minutes until flow stabilizes.
Verify stabilization by observing low variation between cycles in displayed waveforms.
Select acquire mode in ViVitest software.
Click on collect 10 cycles.
From the analyze mode, click on table and save the file.
Save an image of the waveforms using the photo-snap option in ViVitest.
Place the valve holder with the sutured valve inside the glass tube from the custom made assembly.
Sandwich the tube with the top and bottom pieces and secure in-place with lateral screws and nuts.
Average the data collected for each of the waveforms collected, i.e. aortic pressure (AP), ventricular pressure (VP), and flow rate (Q).
Plot the corresponding AP, VP and Q versus time relationships on the same plot for each group of valve (polymer, porcine native aortic valve and bi-leaflet).
Superimpose normal, native aortic valve18, and bi-leaflet prosthetic valve19 plots from the literature for validation purposes.
